_comment: A DOCTRINE, not an enactment, and that is why this subject is the first
under subjects/doctrine/. See docs/directory-conventions.md sections 2 and 3:
enacted law is filed by the authority that enacted it, commercial
instruments by genre. Judge-made law compared ACROSS authorities fits
neither -- no single legislature is constitutive of it, and it is not an
instrument. The grammar this row seeds is subjects/doctrine/<area>/<leaf>/,
with the area vocabulary controlled in subjects/doctrine/AREAS.md, mirroring
contracts/GENRES.md exactly. NOTES.md section 1 argues the case; a reviewer
who disagrees should move the row rather than leave the argument unmade.
THE SUBJECT IS THE DOCTRINE; SINGAPORE IS ITS CENTRE. Chwee Kin Keong v
Digilandmall.com Pte Ltd [2005] SGCA 2 is the reason the subject exists,
and the other three jurisdictions are here to show what its holding is a
departure FROM. They are not independently surveyed and this file does not
claim they are: 'extent' below lists the authorities the encoding reaches,
and 'authority_note' says how each was retrieved and how far it can be
'source' names the primary judgment. The full retrieval record for all four
jurisdictions -- what was fetched, from where, when, and with what integrity
display_name: Unilateral mistake in contract — Singapore's equitable limb, and its common law cousins
citation: Chwee Kin Keong and others v Digilandmall.com Pte Ltd [2005] SGCA 2, [2005] 1 SLR(R) 502 (Singapore Court of Appeal)
authority: Supreme Court of Singapore, Court of Appeal

authority_note.SG: Primary. Chwee Kin Keong v Digilandmall.com Pte Ltd [2005] SGCA 2, retrieved in full and quoted directly; restated in Quoine Pte Ltd v B2C2 Ltd [2020] SGCA(I) 02, also retrieved in full.
authority_note.GB-EAW: Secondary. Hartog, Smith v Hughes, Riverlate and Great Peace Shipping are quoted AS CHARACTERISED BY the Singapore Court of Appeal in Chwee Kin Keong. The English reports were not retrieved.
authority_note.AU: Secondary. Taylor v Johnson (1983) 151 CLR 422 is quoted AS CHARACTERISED BY Chwee Kin Keong at [72] and [73]. The Commonwealth Law Reports were not retrieved. Two open readings are recorded as forks F-AU1 and F-AU2.
authority_note.US: Secondary, and not a jurisdiction's law at all. Restatement (Second) of Contracts sections 153 and 154 are quoted from Donovan v RRL Corp (2001) 26 Cal 4th 261, a public judicial opinion that adopted section 153(a) as California law. The Restatement binds nobody until a State adopts it; see fork F-US1.

source.note: The doctrine has no enactment and therefore no in-force date and no revised edition. It is stated as at the date of the latest decision this corpus reaches, Quoine Pte Ltd v B2C2 Ltd [2020] SGCA(I) 02 (24 February 2020), and no sweep for later Singapore authority has been performed -- see registers/external-modifications.json, which records that omission as an unmet obligation rather than as an absence of findings.
